title: What defined oil, gas and power trading in 2026? | Wood Mackenzie
gist: A Wood Mackenzie teaser for a gated year-end trading guide. It says Middle East conflict defined energy trading in 2026: disruption in the Strait of Hormuz, Brent at US$100/bbl, demand destruction and extreme crack-spread volatility in oil; attacks on Ras Laffan, soaring gas prices and shifting LNG flows in gas; and changing fuel economics, nuclear policy and renewable supply-chain risks in power. The full analysis is behind a download form, so the text gives only headline signals.

themes.theme: Middle East conflict as 2026's market driver

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie says conflict in the Middle East was the defining shock for energy markets in 2026. It disrupted production and exports, restricted critical trade routes and damaged energy infrastructure, with effects across oil, gas, LNG and power markets.
insights.speaker: Stephen Ryan
insights.so_what: A single geopolitical shock moved every energy commodity at once, so cross-commodity correlation and risk to trade routes belong at the centre of 2027 positioning.
insights.quote: 2026 demonstrated how quickly disruption can reshape global energy markets.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie's view is that 2026 showed energy traders how tightly physical supply, trade flows, inventories, demand and regional market dynamics are linked.
insights.speaker: Stephen Ryan
insights.so_what: Trading desks need integrated data on physical flows and inventories across regions, not price signals from one commodity alone.
insights.quote: the year highlighted the connections between physical supply, trade flows, inventories, demand and regional market dynamics

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie names the Strait of Hormuz disruption, Brent at US$100/bbl, demand destruction and extreme crack-spread volatility as the defining features of oil trading in 2026.
insights.speaker: Stephen Ryan
insights.so_what: Brent at $100 caused demand destruction, and extreme crack-spread volatility made refining margins a major source of trading risk and opportunity alongside crude price direction.
insights.quote: From disruption in the Strait of Hormuz and US$100/bbl Brent to demand destruction and extreme crack-spread volatility.

themes.theme: Gas/LNG: Ras Laffan and security of supply

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie says attacks on Ras Laffan defined gas and LNG trading in 2026. They contributed to soaring global gas prices, changed LNG trade flows and brought renewed focus on security of supply.
insights.speaker: Stephen Ryan
insights.so_what: Damage at a major LNG export hub points to lasting risk premia, rerouted cargoes and policy-driven demand for diversified supply and storage.
insights.quote: From the attacks on Ras Laffan and soaring global gas prices to changing LNG flows and a renewed focus on security of supply.
insights.locator: What defined gas and LNG trading in 2026?

themes.theme: Power: fuel economics, nuclear, renewables risk

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie says the global effects of the Middle East conflict, changing fuel economics, nuclear policy and risks in renewable supply chains shaped power trading in 2026.
insights.speaker: Stephen Ryan
insights.so_what: Higher gas and oil prices reshape the power generation stack. Watch nuclear policy shifts and renewable supply-chain constraints as drivers of power prices and spreads.
insights.quote: From the global repercussions of the Middle East conflict to changing fuel economics, nuclear policy and renewable supply-chain risks.
